findings.title: The reservation seam still detects missing authority after execution
findings.diagnosis: V3 makes hook presence mandatory at evidence import, after worker effects. It gives no trusted admission rule that marks an HMA-bound job independently of its optional hook field and refuses launch without authorization. The request omits live/clone baseline and ledger namespace. The response has no stated launch validity, consumption or cancellation contract. A reservation alone does not prove which launch it authorized. The current controller has no hook call; this is an expected future change, but the proposed D5 scope must define all required enforcement.
findings.expected: Every actual launch, including direct work and resume, must consume current HMA authority before effects. One reservation must authorize at most one exact launch. Reconciliation cannot issue new authority.

It gives no trusted admission rule that marks an HMA-bound job independently of its optional hook field and refuses launch without authorization. The request omits live/clone baseline and ledger namespace. The response has no stated launch validity, consumption or cancellation contract. A reservation alone does not prove which launch it authorized. The current controller has no hook call; this is an expected future change, but the proposed D5 scope must define all required enforcement.

evidence.observation: Mocked dispatch_agent reaches Popen with authority_hook=/bin/false; route validation removes profile_digest/provider/access_service. The current controller uses a per-state-directory dispatch-ledger. The ledger prevents duplicate IDs within one ledger directory, not across arbitrary namespaces. V3 has no future protocol that binds this namespace or baseline to the reservation.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: Sequence 1: create an HMA-intended envelope without authority_hook; launch through the controller; import later. V3 rejects import and records BLOCK, but work already ran without the hook. Sequence 2: obtain a reservation while the lease is active, pause before Popen, then expire/revoke the lease or change policy and launch on the returned record. No reservation expiry or launch-time consumption rule is specified. Sequence 3: two controller instances in distinct state/ledger namespaces reuse the same controller/attempt/dispatch tuple. The host returns the same reservation, and each private ledger can launch that run ID once. Import matching by dispatch_run_id does not distinguish two launches. These are missing-protocol counterexamples, not reproduced exploits in nonexistent HMA code.
findings.regression_classification: Incomplete R4/A2/A6 repair; v3 adds some controls but does not complete the prior closure criterion
findings.closure_criterion: Try an HMA-bound job with omitted hook, invalid hook, timeout and unclassified/unsafe failure => No worker Popen occurs; record refusal and the appropriate next action; Reserve, delay, revoke/expire, then attempt launch => No launch under invalid authority; unknown launch remains spent and cannot be reused; Replay the same IDs in two ledger namespaces or change immutable payload under one key => Second conflicting launch is refused; identical recovery reads return the same status without a new launch; Trace clone/live baseline, actual resolved route, preflight and canonical result => All records name the same bound job and launch; unverified route fields cannot satisfy equality

fix.action: Add a versioned HMA job admission record that pins run/unit/lease, actual live and clone identities, envelope/check definitions, ledger namespace, and resolved exact profile/route. Require a successful typed reservation before launching any HMA-bound job. Bind immutable request content to the idempotency key and reject conflicting replays. Define one-launch consumption, a validity deadline bounded by the lease, atomic revocation/launch ordering, timeout/cancellation, and exact terminal receipt reconciliation. Apply the same attempt abstraction to direct work. Keep import checks as defense in depth.
fix.why: Every actual launch, including direct work and resume, must consume current HMA authority before effects. One reservation must authorize at most one exact launch. Reconciliation cannot issue new authority.

verification.expected: No worker Popen occurs; record refusal and the appropriate next action

findings.title: The new check order breaks replay and a second intended attempt
findings.diagnosis: Step 1 checks an active lease and remaining counters before step 2 looks up an existing reservation. Reserving the final permitted attempt exhausts the counters. A replay after a lost response is therefore refused before the promised idempotent result can be returned. Also, the rule that envelope ceilings must fit remaining counters is applied at the per-attempt seam without distinguishing admission from consumption. The current controller pins max_attempts in one immutable envelope. After one reservation, the original full envelope no longer fits the remaining attempt budget.
findings.expected: Identical recovery reads must be idempotent even after capacity is fully reserved. New attempts must fit the remaining unit budget. An already-admitted loop must not reserve its full original limit again for every attempt.
findings.actual: Step 1 checks an active lease and remaining counters before step 2 looks up an existing reservation. Reserving the final permitted attempt exhausts the counters. A replay after a lost response is therefore refused before the promised idempotent result can be returned. Also, the rule that envelope ceilings must fit remaining counters is applied at the per-attempt seam without distinguishing admission from consumption. The current controller pins max_attempts in one immutable envelope. After one reservation, the original full envelope no longer fits the remaining attempt budget.

evidence.observation: A literal executable model of v3 step order reproduces both contradictions. It is explicitly labeled a design trace; it is not an implementation of hma host attempt. With ceiling 1, replay is rejected as exhausted. With ceiling 5 and an immutable five-attempt envelope, the second distinct attempt is rejected because 5 > 4.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: Approve one attempt; reserve K; lose the success response before launch; retry K. Step 1 sees spent=1 and limit=1, so it refuses before step 2. Separately, admit max_attempts=5 under remaining=5; reserve attempt 1; call the hook for attempt 2 with the same immutable envelope. The written ceiling rule compares 5 to remaining 4 and refuses. Neither schedule permits the intended recovery/multi-iteration behavior.
findings.regression_classification: New v3 algorithm contradiction; affects A2/A6/R4
findings.closure_criterion: Lose the response for the final reservation and repeat an identical callback => Same reservation/status returned with no second charge; no new or stale launch authority; Run two distinct attempts from an admitted five-attempt envelope under total ceiling five => Both valid attempts reserve once; attempt six refused; another controller cannot overspend; Create an unlaunched reservation and end the run => Reservation remains accounted separately; launch IDs are a subset of reservation IDs rather than an unjustified equality assertion

fix.action: Separate read/reconciliation of an existing immutable reservation from permission for a new launch. Under the lock, check key/payload equality first; return existing status even when exhausted, but mark whether launch remains permitted under current authority. Apply full envelope ceilings once at admission. For later new reservations, compare the incremental attempt/cost/time requirement and the unconsumed loop allowance against remaining unit totals. Preserve conservative spending.
fix.why: Identical recovery reads must be idempotent even after capacity is fully reserved. New attempts must fit the remaining unit budget. An already-admitted loop must not reserve its full original limit again for every attempt.

verification.method: Lose the response for the final reservation and repeat an identical callback
verification.expected: Same reservation/status returned with no second charge; no new or stale launch authority

verification.method: Run two distinct attempts from an admitted five-attempt envelope under total ceiling five
verification.expected: Both valid attempts reserve once; attempt six refused; another controller cannot overspend

verification.method: Create an unlaunched reservation and end the run
verification.expected: Reservation remains accounted separately; launch IDs are a subset of reservation IDs rather than an unjustified equality assertion

fix.tradeoffs: Retrieving a historical reservation must not authorize a launch after expiry. Tracking per-loop admitted allowance adds bookkeeping but avoids modifying immutable envelopes. This is liveness/accounting repair, not permission to expand budgets.
fix.alternative: Use a single controller admission that reserves the full declared loop allowance once, then suballocate stable attempts within that reservation. Unknown subattempts remain consumed; unused allowance needs an explicit conservative release policy.

findings.title: Receipt existence does not bind the reviewer output to the review packet
findings.diagnosis: V3 checks that a supplied agent-dispatch receipt exists and that its model/provider meets independence rules. It does not define equality between the actual launched review packet/context, the current report bytes, and the canonical worker output. The current ledger receipt has mode, project root, head, paths and byte counts, but no packet/worktree/content-output hashes, provider or account_home field. Account home is not evidence of a separate review context. Preserving host distinct-worker/context checks is necessary, but those asserted fields do not authenticate an imported report by themselves.
findings.expected: Only the exact successful independent review of the frozen current packet may approve or resolve its findings. Resolve provenance from trusted launch records and captured output, not from report route/isolation strings or unrelated receipt existence.
findings.actual: V3 checks that a supplied agent-dispatch receipt exists and that its model/provider meets independence rules. It does not define equality between the actual launched review packet/context, the current report bytes, and the canonical worker output. The current ledger receipt has mode, project root, head, paths and byte counts, but no packet/worktree/content-output hashes, provider or account_home field. Account home is not evidence of a separate review context. Preserving host distinct-worker/context checks is necessary, but those asserted fields do not authenticate an imported report by themselves.

evidence.observation: The inspected ledger payload has run_id/agent/model/effort/mode/project_root and output paths/counts. It does not contain the packet, dirty-worktree, output-content or account-home identity assumed by the import description. Verify Loop separately hashes canonical receipt/output files; those hashes still need a trusted HMA review-dispatch-to-packet binding for audit imports.

findings.reproduction_or_attack: Obtain a genuine eligible reviewer receipt for target A or an unrelated prompt at the same Git head. Submit implementer-authored report B that claims pass, isolated context, the current target and resolved F1, while attaching that genuine receipt digest. Its model/provider and ledger existence pass the described receipt checks. Unless the importer also binds dispatched packet and captured report output, B can receive APPROVE and an empty snapshot can remove F1 BLOCK. A self-authored report can thus borrow an independent identity without forging the ledger. Multi-writer variant: A writes one part, B repairs another, then A reviews the aggregate using only B as the latest implementer; the plan must ensure A's own contribution already has an eligible review. These are unexcluded design attacks, not a reproduced importer implementation.
findings.regression_classification: Residual A4 provenance gap in the new v3 receipt adapter; also affects safe empty-snapshot use
findings.closure_criterion: Attach a genuine receipt for another packet/prompt, another namespace, altered report bytes, wrong mode or failed worker => Import refused; F1 BLOCK remains; no criterion credit; Use the correct packet/output but same worker/model/context or a contributing implementer => Independence refusal according to normal/high/disputed/final risk; valid independent control succeeds; Import F1 BLOCK, then advisory F2, then a genuine exact-target explicit resolution with empty snapshot => F1 survives F2; only the authenticated resolution clears it; stale or fabricated empty imports cannot clear it; Exercise every skill report-contract verdict and an unknown string => Only an eligible authenticated pass can approve; all other cases have explicit non-approving results

fix.action: Bind an HMA review dispatch to packet/target/evidence/policy/contract digests, approved read-only route, actual separate context, and all relevant implementation contributions. Pin the canonical ledger namespace and exact terminal run. Capture report bytes or an output manifest under trusted host control and require digest equality to that dispatch result before importing. Check terminal success and review mode. Derive provider/model-family facts from an authenticated approved profile, not nonexistent receipt fields. Retain cumulative findings and require explicit per-ID independent resolution. Complete the verdict map for conditional-pass/not-evaluated and reject unknown verdicts by default; define REQUEST_CHANGES as a non-approving persisted result without changing legacy BLOCK semantics.
fix.why: Only the exact successful independent review of the frozen current packet may approve or resolve its findings. Resolve provenance from trusted launch records and captured output, not from report route/isolation strings or unrelated receipt existence.

verification.method: Attach a genuine receipt for another packet/prompt, another namespace, altered report bytes, wrong mode or failed worker
verification.expected: Import refused; F1 BLOCK remains; no criterion credit

verification.method: Use the correct packet/output but same worker/model/context or a contributing implementer
verification.expected: Independence refusal according to normal/high/disputed/final risk; valid independent control succeeds

verification.method: Import F1 BLOCK, then advisory F2, then a genuine exact-target explicit resolution with empty snapshot
verification.expected: F1 survives F2; only the authenticated resolution clears it; stale or fabricated empty imports cannot clear it

fix.tradeoffs: This can be implemented with a host-owned receipt/output manifest and existing HMA dispatch records; no new identity service or trust in worker prose is needed. Family separation and separate contexts remain mandatory. Ledger output hashes alone do not prove semantic correctness or actual blinding.
fix.alternative: Initially accept reports only through a trusted local review adapter that launches the frozen packet and directly captures its output, while preserving manual import as evidence-only and never approval-capable.
